To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. the ocular vascular permeabilities of rabbits treated with nitrogen mustard or CVF are not significantly different from those of untreated controls; 2. the chemotactic activities in aqueous humor of both treated and untreated rabbits are partially heat-sensitive and are not inhibited by C5a; and 3. these activities are attracted by rabbit PMNs but not by human PMNs.

the intravitreous administration of Escherichiacolli endotoxin to rabbits induces a marked increase in the permeability of ocular blood vessels, and that this increase is independent of circulating polymorphonuclear neutrophils and complement.

the vascular permeability of ocular tissues following the intraocular injection of an endotoxic bacterial cell wall component (lipopolysaccharide) is determined neither by polymorphonuclear neutrophils nor by complement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism by which the ocular inflammatory response to intravitreous bacterial endotoxin occurs and the role of complement and polymorphonucleated leukocytes in this response.
the mechanism of the vascular permeability response in the eye to endotoxin and the role of PMNs.

understanding the mechanism of ocular vascular permeabilization in response to intraocular inflammation, specifically, the role of polymorphonuclear neutrophils, complement, and complement-derived chemotactic factor(s).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the OVP following intraocular LPS is not determined by PMNs or by complement.
LPS, a potent activator of the alternative complement pathway, is not an important activator of this pathway in the eye.
the ocular vascular permeabilizing activity of LPS is not determined by the presence of PMNs or complement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the OVP induced by intraocular injection of LPS is not dependent upon the presence of either PMNs or complement.
the ocular vascular permeabilizing effect of endotoxin in the rabbit eye does not appear to be mediated by PMN's or by circulating complement.

the ocular inflammatory response induced by intravitreous endotoxin is not mediated by complement, is only partly dependent on polymorphonuclear cells, and that a noncomplement-derived chemotactic factor may be important in the inflammatory response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ocular vascular permeabilty (OVP) induced by intraocular endotoxin is not mediated by polymorphonuclear cells or complement.
the complement system and polymorphonucleated cells do not appear to be the main drivers of the vascular permeability that occurs following intravitreol LPS.
the vascular permeability response to LPS is not dependent on complement and PMN infiltration, and that the inflammatory response to LPS in the eye is not a typical PMN response.
